name: Diablo — Act 1
statusNote: A playable, winnable slice, still in development. A personal fan tribute, deliberately kept out of any commercial framing.
oneLiner: A single-file canvas ARPG tribute to Diablo II's Act 1 — Rogue Encampment through Blood Moor and the Den of Evil to the Blood Raven boss fight, with three playable classes.

components.name: Data tables
components.desc: CLASSES (Sorceress, Barbarian, Amazon with real stat spreads and 4-skill kits), SKILLS (9 across projectile/spread/nova/melee/leap), MON (five monster types incl. the boss), BASES (per-class item bases).

components.name: Zone system
components.desc: Four hand-authored zone builders (town, moor, den, burial), each placing monster packs procedurally while guaranteeing a clear entry point.

components.name: Combat / skills
components.desc: tryCast() validates cooldown and mana, then branches on skill kind.

components.name: Enemy AI
components.desc: Per-monster aggro/range/attack-cooldown state machine; the Fallen Shaman heals allies, Blood Raven is a dedicated boss.

components.name: Loot and progression
components.desc: Chance-gated drops (guaranteed on the boss), stat and skill points on level-up and quest completion.

components.name: Render chain
components.desc: Zone, decorations, torches, NPCs, monsters, projectiles, items, particles, HUD, and overlay screens.

dataFlow: Left-click is context-sensitive move-or-attack; right-click casts the bound skill; 1/2/3 rebind it; Q/E potions; I/C panels.
update(dt) advances zone timers and runs monster AI (aggro, chase, attack).
tryCast resolves through the cooldown/mana gate and spawns the effect.
Projectile and melee collisions resolve; deaths drop loot and XP, possibly leveling.
Zone-exit collision transitions to the next zone.
The render chain paints the frame and rAF reschedules.
integrations: None beyond the browser — fully self-contained, no shared code with the other games
decisions: A prominent IP-tribute disclaimer: a personal fan tribute, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard; the MIT license explicitly excludes referenced IP.
Kept out of commercial framing deliberately — it showcases range without IP risk.
Safe-zone spawn generation is a deliberate nod to D2's own map-generation discipline.
The skill system mirrors D2's class-identity structure (one primary + a 3-skill kit) rather than a generic combo system.
